subject: ventures/fishing-charter-trip-pricing-calculator
professional: an owner-operator charter captain (USCG OUPV / six-pack or Master licence) who sets next season's half-day and full-day rate card; first checks: is the break-even right once weather days are counted, does the 'take home' figure mean after tax, can it split fixed costs across half-day and full-day trips, does it stop a per-angler quote above six passengers on an uninspected boat, and does the trips-needed warning compare like with like

evidence.correctness: Recomputed by hand in Python from a cost-plus charter pricing build-up written without the author's tests (fuel = hours x gph x $/gal; variable = fuel + deckhand + bait; fixed spread over completed trips = booked x (1 - cancel); gross-up for card fee by dividing by 1 - fee), then compared with the shipped calc.mjs via /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/a8fec2a0-187e-5564-ad4f-f522fdb134ed/scratchpad/fc/re.mjs. Sample (6 h, 14 gph, $4.25, $150 deckhand, $60 bait, $21,000 fixed, 90 booked, 20% weather, 3% fee, $40,000 target): fuel 357.00, variable 567.00, completed 72, target price 1,457.96, break-even 885.22, per angler (4) 364.49: all match. Weather add (price at 72 completed minus price at 90) 174.68: matches. Fuel swing 84 gal / 0.97 = 86.60: matches. At $800 now: annual result -5,952.00: matches. One logic error: the trips-needed warning compares completed trips needed with trips booked (calc.mjs:71). At $1,400 now it needs 77.1 completed trips (96.4 bookings at 20% weather) against 72 completed / 90 booked, so the target is missed but the warning is suppressed because 77.1 < 90; at $800 it says '292 completed trips ... more than the 90 you expect to book' when the bookings needed are 365. Core prices right; one finding wrong.
evidence.completeness: Claimed features checked end to end in Chromium (Playwright over a local http server, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/a8fec2a0-187e-5564-ad4f-f522fdb134ed/scratchpad/fc/pw.cjs): Load an example -> 'Price for your target: $1,457.96 a trip. Break-even: $885.22', 5 volume-sweep rows, 5 findings, zero console errors; blank trip length -> named error and report hidden; usage counter wrote {"example_loaded":1} to localStorage; summary text and CSV builders run in tests. Break-even, target price, per-angler price, current-price check, weather effect and fuel effect all present as the README says. No stubs or TODOs. Leftover: SAMPLE.fuelSurchargeFrom (calc.mjs:7) is an input that nothing reads or shows.
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/fishing-charter-trip-pricing-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 21 tests, 21 pass, 0.12 s; the README's repo-root command also passes 21/21. Five mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: two caught (fee gross-up divide -> multiply; annual result over booked instead of completed trips), three survived: the weather-effect baseline (priceFor over booked -> completed, so the finding reports $0.00), the target-miss finding inverted (gap < 0 -> gap > 0), and the 15% weather threshold moved to 50%. The findings a captain reads are untested apart from the high loss finding and the trips-needed text.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (101 lines), index.html, usage.mjs and the three test files. Pure functions, no dependencies, a guarded localStorage counter with a persistent opt-out, escaped HTML in findings, labelled inputs. Defects: anglers and current price silently drop typed text ('4 anglers', 'eight hundred' -> NaN -> treated as blank, no error, calc.mjs:35-36) while every other field reports it; fractional anglers (2.5) accepted; dollars() is a dense IIFE one-liner (calc.mjs:17); an unused SAMPLE key (calc.mjs:7).
evidence.claims: Backed: no-warranty and not-advice disclaimer in the footer (index.html:115) and README; 'nothing is sent' backed by page.test.mjs:264 (no fetch/XHR/beacon) and the module-import test; usage tracking described accurately (four local-only events, DNT/GPC respected, opt-out button, usage.mjs); the stated pricing rule (index.html:94) is exactly what calc.mjs computes; 'does not know what other captains charge' is honest. served-copy.mjs reports no stale origin in llms.txt/sitemap/robots/canonicals after the deploy rewrite. Not backed: the target field is labelled 'Profit you want to take home per year' (index.html:69) and README says it 'pays you', but the maths treats it as pre-tax business profit; self-employment and income tax are not mentioned anywhere (the 'Not decided' list names only sales or occupancy tax), so a captain entering a true take-home figure under-prices by the tax on it. The fuel finding says each $1/gal 'changes the cost of a trip by' 86.60 when the cost changes by 84.00 and 86.60 is the price change (calc.mjs:77).
evidence.fitness: Job walked: a captain setting next season's half-day and full-day rates (VENTURE.yaml names this as the first visitor). The tool prices one trip type at a time and spreads all yearly fixed costs over that type's bookings, so running it once for 50 half-days and once for 40 full-days charges the full $21,000 to each, over-pricing both; there is no way to split fixed costs across a mix, which is the core of a rate card. Maintenance is only a yearly fixed figure, so engine-hour wear (service intervals, repower reserve) does not scale with trip length or count. Usable for a single-product captain as a sanity check on break-even; a multi-trip-type rate card needs hand allocation first.
evidence.domain: Compared with standard owner-operator cost-plus pricing (variable cost per trip + fixed costs over realised trips + owner draw, grossed up for card fees) the method is sound and the weather effect is modelled correctly. Departures a captain would hit: no passenger cap; USCG rules (46 U.S.C. 2101, 'uninspected passenger vessel', and the OUPV six-pack licence) limit an uninspected boat to six passengers for hire, but 12 anglers yields a $121.50 per-angler quote with no warning; no mixed trip types sharing fixed costs; maintenance and engine reserve not per engine hour; card fee has no per-transaction part (e.g. 2.9% + $0.30); retained weather deposits not modelled though the finding recommends a deposit policy; income/self-employment tax on the owner's draw not mentioned.

defects.what: The trips-needed warning compares completed trips needed with trips booked: at $1,400 a trip the target needs 77.1 completed trips (96.4 bookings at 20% weather) against 72 completed / 90 booked, yet no warning shows because 77.1 < 90; at $800 it reports 292 completed trips 'more than the 90 you expect to book' when 365 bookings are needed.

The target is labelled 'Profit you want to take home per year' but is treated as pre-tax business profit; income and self-employment tax are not mentioned (the Not-decided list names only sales or occupancy tax), so a captain entering a real take-home figure under-prices.
One trip type per run with all yearly fixed costs: a half-day plus full-day rate card (the first visitor's job in VENTURE.yaml) double-counts fixed costs unless the captain splits them by hand.
No passenger cap or warning: 12 anglers gives a per-angler quote though an uninspected passenger vessel run under an OUPV (six-pack) licence may carry at most 6 passengers for hire (46 U.S.C. 2101).

Three of five seeded mutants survive: the weather-effect baseline, the target-miss finding condition and the 15% weather threshold are untested, so the findings a captain reads can break with every test green.
Anglers and current price silently drop typed text ('4 anglers', 'eight hundred' become blank with no error) and accept fractional anglers, unlike every other field.
The fuel finding says each $1/gal 'changes the cost of a trip by' $86.60; the cost changes by $84.00 (gallons per trip) and $86.60 is the price change after the card-fee gross-up.
Maintenance and engine reserve only as a yearly fixed figure (no per-engine-hour cost); card fee has no per-transaction part; retained weather deposits not modelled.
SAMPLE carries fuelSurchargeFrom, an input nothing reads or shows (dead field).

verdict: A small, honest cost-plus calculator whose core numbers are right: target price $1,457.96, break-even $885.22, weather effect $174.68, fuel swing $86.60 and the -$5,952 annual result at $800 all match a hand build-up, and the page works in a browser with the disclaimer and local-only usage counting it describes. It does not meet the bar. The trips-needed warning compares completed trips with booked trips, so it is silent at $1,400 when the target is missed. The 'take home' target is really pre-tax. Three of five seeded mutants in the findings logic survive. A captain's real job, a half-day and full-day rate card sharing one boat's fixed costs within the six-passenger limit, is not modelled. Fixing calc.mjs:71 (compare with completed trips, report bookings), relabelling the target as pre-tax profit, adding a six-passenger warning and testing the findings would lift claims and verification to 3.
